findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/59-nineteenth-after-pentecost/sections/homily/10-homily.tex, opening sentence of the Cross movement (line 96), 'St Augustine hears that verse differently', which follows the movement break after Hilary's quotation of Mt 25:35, 'I was hungry, and you gave me to eat' (line 92)
findings.problem: In speech, 'that verse' first attaches to the last verse the assembly heard, Mt 25:35, and not to the Gradual's Ps 140:2, which was quoted four sentences earlier. The listener recovers the referent only in the next sentence, when Augustine's 'evening sacrifice' arrives. A reader can look back on the page; a listener cannot, so the new movement opens on a misreference across a pause.
findings.required_result: Name the verse when the movement begins, for example 'St Augustine hears the Gradual's verse differently: first of Christ, ...', and leave the rest of the movement unchanged.

findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/59-nineteenth-after-pentecost/sections/homily/10-homily.tex, second movement (lines 41-42), 'This morning's Collect asks for the freedom to do it'
findings.problem: The spoken body has to be speakable verbatim at any Mass of this Sunday. 'This morning' is false when the homily is preached at a later Mass of the day, such as an afternoon or evening Sunday Mass, so the preacher would have to edit the text before reading it. The note gives the occasion only as the Mass of 4 October 2026, with no hour.
findings.required_result: Use a time-neutral phrase such as 'Today's Collect' or 'The Collect of this Mass', and leave the rest of the sentence unchanged.

findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/59-nineteenth-after-pentecost/sections/homily/90-note.tex, 'Exact loci' (lines 53-55: 'Gradual, Ps 140:2', 'Communion, Ps 118:4-5', '... and Ps 138:16') and References, Douay-Rheims entry (line 73: 'Ps 118:4-5; 138:16; 140:2')
findings.problem: guidance/liturgy/roman-1962-propers.md ('Source Records and Text Control') requires psalm citations in the Missal's Vulgate numbering, 'with the common modern number in parentheses where it differs'. All three psalms the note cites differ: they are 119, 139 and 141 in the modern numbering. The note gives none of the modern numbers and does not say its numbering is the Vulgate's. A reader who checks Ps 140:2 or Ps 138:16 in a modern Bible finds other psalms. The note's own Augustine reference does give the other numbering ('Psalms CXIX and CXLI in that translation'), so the apparatus is inconsistent with itself. STU-009(c) records the same class of defect in the study as advisory.
findings.required_result: Add the modern number in parentheses at the first citation of each psalm in the note and in the References: Ps 140:2 (141:2), Ps 118:4-5 (119:4-5) and Ps 138:16 (139:16).

observations.note: The checker requires the homily component to declare every element key. guidance/liturgy/propers-three-documents.md, however, lets the homily leave minor propers to the research 'without reciting an inventory of every minor proper', and this homily's note leaves the Alleluia, Offertory and Secret to the studies. The manifest therefore declares a coverage that the speech does not have and is not required to have. That points to a missing distinction between 'informed by' and 'covers' for homily components in the checker or the profile, not to a defect in this leaf.

summary: Cold review of the homily 'The Nineteenth Sunday after Pentecost: Clothed for the Wedding' (src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/59-nineteenth-after-pentecost/homily.tex with sections/homily/10-homily.tex and 90-note.tex). All ten sealed input hashes matched REVIEW_INPUTS before reading. The spoken body was read through continuously as a listener would hear it, then checked against the contract, the reviewed studies and the sources. It makes one clear exegetical argument. The guest already inside lacks the garment the King looks for. That garment is charity, the Bridegroom's own (Gregory), the new man who is Christ (Jerome), shown in the Epistle's four acts and the lifted hands, and asked for as grace in the Communion's 'O that'. The argument moves from the Cross to the altar, from the two feasts to three practicable acts, and ends in hope and a return to the opening 'Friend'. It speaks the study's two kept disagreements: Augustine against Hilary on the evening sacrifice, and Hilary's baptismal gift beside Gregory's and Augustine's charity. It keeps the bounds in interpretations.md 4.5. It does not call the wedding feast the Eucharist in a Father's name, and it does not identify the highways. It uses no other Mass, commentator or compilation fact. There is no anecdote, personal experience or clerical identity, and it contains no composed prayer. The one verse it commends for prayer is the exact Douay Ps 118:5. Evidence checked at locus: every quoted span against the tracked Challoner verse tables, the Cummiskey 1861 payload (e13f1baa...), NPNF1-6 Sermo 90 sections 1, 4, 5 and 9 and Sermo 95 section 7, NPNF1-8 Enarr. in Ps. 118 Aleph 5 and 140 section 3, and NPNF1-10 Hom. 69 in Matth.; all were found. Gregory Hom. 38 sections 9 and 11-14 (including the Ps 138:16 hope for the imperfect in section 12) were checked in the tracked Wikisource Latin, and Hilary on Ps 140:2-3 and Mt 22:11 in the tracked PL 9 layer. Jerome PL 26 cols. 160 D and 508 C were read on page images of the registered scan, fetched again with its digest matched. Every paraphrase is faithful. The spoken count was recomputed at 1,453 words. That is 11.2-12.1 minutes at 120-130 words a minute, within the approximate 10-12, and the note truthfully says that no delivery was timed. Quotation density was weighed: about 27 per cent of spoken words are quoted, and five Fathers are named. The quotations are judged to serve one argument carried in the preacher's plain voice, not a lecture assembled from quotations. Limits: Gregory and Hilary were checked on text layers rather than page images, no audible rehearsal was possible, and typesetting is left to visual review. Verdict: PASS, with three advisories. One is an oral misreference, one a time-bound phrase, and one missing modern psalm numbers in the note.
